 The Nepal Premier League (NPL) 2026 reaches its conclusion on Saturday, November 21, with the same two teams that contested for the title almost a year ago meeting again in Kirtipur.
 Sudur Paschim Royals face defending champions Lumbini Lions at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground, where Lumbini won the 2025 final by six wickets after bowling the Royals out for 85.

 For Sudur Paschim, this is a third successive final and a third attempt at a first NPL title, having also lost the inaugural decider to Janakpur Bolts by five wickets in December 2024. Rohit Paudel's Lumbini side have beaten them twice already in this edition.
 The Sporting News has a look at how to watch the NPL 2026 final between Sudur Paschim Royals and Lumbini Lions, starting time and television channel in India.

 Nepal Premier League final 2026 live stream, TV channel
 Here's how to watch Sudur Paschim Royals vs. Lumbini Lions in India:
 TV channel: Star Sports Network
 Live stream:  FanCode
 In India, Star Sports Network channels will provide the live broadcast of the NPL 2026 final, with live streaming available through the FanCode app and website.
 What time is Nepal Premier League final 2026?
 The Nepal Premier League 2026 final will be played on Saturday, November 21, 2026 , at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur, Kathmandu, the venue that has staged every match of the tournament.
 The match is scheduled to begin at 4:30 p.m. NPT, which translates to 4:15 p.m. IST for viewers in India . 
 Sudur Paschim Royals vs. Lumbini Lions: Key players to watch
 Dipendra Singh Airee carries the Royals' batting and showed it in Qualifier 1, where his 52 from 51 balls was the only half-century in a total of 105 for 8 and included the innings' sole six.
 Around him, Scott Kuggeleijn and Tharindu Rathnayake have given Misbah-ul-Haq's side the control that took them past Chitwan, while Haider Ali and Brandon McMullen are the overseas batters capable of changing the tempo at the top.
 Lumbini's case rests on Niroshan Dickwella and Ruben Trumpelmann, who was named player of the match in last year's final and has now produced a decisive spell in a knockout game in consecutive seasons.
 D'Arcy Short was bowled third ball in Qualifier 1 and remains the one Lumbini batter yet to deliver a significant innings in the playoffs, which matters on a Kirtipur surface where 130 has been a competitive total throughout this tournament.
